fixes.find: I'm wearing a striped sailor's shirt and a canvas storm jacket. Grandma kept the jacket in her trunk until she died, and then Dad gave it to me and said, "Granddad's, I think."
fixes.replace: I'm wearing a striped sailor's undershirt and a canvas storm jacket. Grandma kept the jacket in her trunk until she died, and then Dad gave it to me and said, "Must be Granddad's."
fixes.why: Glossary: first mention is a striped sailor's undershirt; the quoted line has a set rendering.

fixes.find: I'm wearing a striped sailor's shirt and Granddad's storm jacket, darned at the elbow.
fixes.replace: I'm wearing a striped sailor's undershirt and Granddad's storm jacket, darned at the elbow.
fixes.why: This branch can be the first mention of the telnyashka; glossary asks for undershirt.

fixes.find: For fifty-four years I lived by the sea, where the water is warm as a bath, and I taught people myself how not to drown in it.
fixes.replace: For fifty-four years I lived by the sea, where the water is warm as a bath, and I was the one teaching people how not to drown in it.
fixes.why: "Taught people myself how" is a Russian-order calque.

fixes.find: These are my third pair of boots on the road.
fixes.replace: This is my third pair of boots on the road.
fixes.why: Agreement: pair is singular.

fixes.find: Under the riverbed, six hundred meters or so beneath my feet, run the old workings of the Glubokaya.
fixes.replace: Under the riverbed, six hundred meters or so beneath my feet, run the old workings of the Glubokaya mine.
fixes.why: Glossary: Glubokaya needs "mine" for English readers.

fixes.find: "All my life I handed you out light," she says. "I'll hand it out today too. Bring it back."
fixes.replace: "I gave you light all my life," she says. "I'll give it today too. Bring it back."
fixes.why: "Handed you out light" is not idiomatic English.

fixes.find: "Pa. I'm here. I wait."
fixes.replace: "Pa. I'm here. I'm waiting."
fixes.why: The Russian line is careful but grammatical; broken English adds an error.

fixes.find: "Grandpa, there's perch here," he whispers. "Only quiet."
fixes.replace: "Grandpa, there are perch here," he whispers. "Just be quiet."
fixes.why: Plural agreement and "Only quiet" are calqued.

fixes.find: a stack of five-thousand notes.
fixes.replace: a stack of five-thousand-ruble notes.
fixes.why: English needs the currency; otherwise the realia is unclear.

fixes.find: from the shaft of the bootleg pit.
fixes.replace: from the shaft of a wildcat pit.
fixes.why: Glossary: копанка is a wildcat pit, not a bootleg pit.

fixes.find: the numbers on it stand at thirty meters.
fixes.replace: the readout is stuck at thirty meters.
fixes.why: "Numbers stand at" is a Russian collocation.

fixes.find: A man's watch on a steel bracelet, a Shturmanskie, with a little star on the dial.
fixes.replace: A man's watch on a steel bracelet, a Shturmanskie watch, a Soviet navigator's watch, with a little star on the dial.
fixes.why: Glossary asks for the explanation at first possible mention.

fixes.find: the bracelet slips off my wrist, and I don't manage to catch it.
fixes.replace: the bracelet slips off my wrist, and I can't catch it in time.
fixes.why: "Don't manage to" is stiff here; the Russian means he is too late.

fixes.find: I come out from under the snag in 1996
fixes.replace: I surface from under the snag in 1996
fixes.why: He is emerging from underwater; "surface" keeps the action precise.

fixes.find: A steel bracelet hangs out of the fist
fixes.replace: A steel bracelet hangs from his fist
fixes.why: "Hangs out of the fist" is not idiomatic.

fixes.find: Beside us on her knees is a girl of about seven, panama hat in her fist, lips blue, counting out loud.
fixes.replace: Beside us, on her knees, is a girl of about seven, a little sunhat in her fist, lips blue, counting aloud.
fixes.why: Russian панамка is a child's sunhat here, not an English Panama hat.

fixes.find: "One hundred ninety," she says. "One hundred ninety-one."
fixes.replace: "One hundred and ninety," she says. "One hundred and ninety-one."
fixes.why: Glossary says children's counting keeps "and".

fixes.find: The blood coming from it is pink with water.
fixes.replace: Water thins the blood pink.
fixes.why: The original image is physical; the English phrasing is clumsy.

fixes.find: My chest suddenly cramps, as if from a ball in the stomach.
fixes.replace: My chest suddenly cramps, as if I'd taken a ball to the gut.
fixes.why: "Мяч под дых" is a blow that knocks the breath out, not a ball in the stomach.

fixes.find: and my palm burns, as if it had somewhere to lie.
fixes.replace: and my palm burns, as if it knows where it belongs.
fixes.why: Literal rendering of "есть куда лечь" does not work in English.

fixes.find: I press on his chest, hard, like a ball in the stomach.
fixes.replace: I press on his chest, hard, the way a ball knocks the breath out of you.
fixes.why: Same idiom: the force is like being hit in the solar plexus.

fixes.find: "Two hundred," I say along with her. "Two hundred one."
fixes.replace: "Two hundred," I say along with her. "Two hundred and one."
fixes.why: Keeps the established counting style with "and".

fixes.find: We really, really need to not lose count.
fixes.replace: We need, very badly, not to lose count.
fixes.why: The double "really" sounds modern and flat for this tense adult voice.

fixes.find: hold it on her knees
fixes.replace: hold it in her lap
fixes.why: English says "in her lap," not "on her knees."

fixes.find: The girl with the panama hat in her fist looks at me with round eyes.
fixes.replace: The girl with the little sunhat in her fist looks at me with round eyes.
fixes.why: Панамка is a child's sunhat here; "Panama hat" misleads.

fixes.find: Nobody in this city knows this old man, and nobody ever will.
fixes.replace: Nobody in this city knows this old man, and nobody will recognize him.
fixes.why: "Не узнает" means recognize, not get to know him later.

fixes.find: The bluff over the riverbed is the same, and the Gorka is the same, and the comet is the same.
fixes.replace: The bluff over the riverbed is the same, Krasnaya Gorka is the same, and the comet is the same.
fixes.why: "The Gorka" is opaque in English; the glossary form is Krasnaya Gorka.

fixes.find: But the streetlights up top run wrong, and beyond the bluff burn the lights of a street I don't remember.
fixes.replace: But the lights up top move in unfamiliar ways, and beyond the bluff, the lights of a street I don't remember are burning.
fixes.why: "Фонари ходят" are moving lights, not streetlights that "run."

fixes.find: Now in 2061 stands a life that resembles mine the way a cousin does.
fixes.replace: Now, in 2061, there is a life that resembles mine the way a cousin does.
fixes.why: Russian inversion sounds unnatural in English.

fixes.find: The number I know by heart answers there in a stranger's sleepy voice
fixes.replace: The number I know by heart is answered by a stranger's sleepy voice
fixes.why: A phone number does not "answer there" in idiomatic English.

fixes.find: Mom, who's running here across the waste ground right now in her work overalls.
fixes.replace: Mom, who's running here across the vacant lot right now in her work overalls.
fixes.why: "Waste ground" reads British; "vacant lot" is neutral American English.

fixes.find: They don't know anything yet, about the dust or the hospital.
fixes.replace: They don't know yet about the dust or the hospital.
fixes.why: The comma makes the sentence sag and over-explain.

fixes.find: I feel I could hold it a while longer.
fixes.replace: I could hold it a while longer.
fixes.why: Filter verb; the sentence is stronger without announcing the feeling.

fixes.find: Here, in 1996, I won't have the Choir; the seam will go and take it with it.
fixes.replace: Here, in 1996, I won't have the Choir; the seam will close and take it with it.
fixes.why: "The seam will go" is too literal and weak in English.

fixes.find: Go back nowhere. Leave for the worlds where I don't grow old
fixes.replace: Don't go back anywhere. Leave for the worlds where I don't grow old
fixes.why: Choice text is visible to the player; "go back nowhere" is not idiomatic.

fixes.find: I can no longer stretch out mine.
fixes.replace: I can't reach out my own.
fixes.why: "Stretch out mine" is stiff and unidiomatic for a hand.

fixes.find: My heart is racing like an engine started with a push.
fixes.replace: My heart is racing like a push-started engine.
fixes.why: More idiomatic English for the same механика image.

fixes.find: I'm seventy-two; headfirst is no longer for me, and the boy is down there by the snag, and the girl is already counting.
fixes.replace: I'm seventy-two; I can't go headfirst anymore, and the boy is down there by the snag, and the girl is already counting.
fixes.why: "Headfirst is no longer for me" is a Russian-shaped phrase.

fixes.find: walk home barefoot, from old memory, to where I lived.
fixes.replace: walk home barefoot by memory, to the place where I lived.
fixes.why: "From old memory" is not idiomatic English.

fixes.find: The entrance is the same, but the door is different, steel, with a code I don't know.
fixes.replace: The building entrance is the same, but the door is different, steel, with a code I don't know.
fixes.why: Подъезд needs a little anchoring for English readers.

fixes.find: A woman in a housecoat comes out with a trash bag and looks at me the way you look at drunks.
fixes.replace: A woman in a housecoat comes out with a trash bag and looks at me the way people look at drunks.
fixes.why: Generic "you" pulls the reader in too directly; the Russian is impersonal.

fixes.find: and the curtains there have flowers on them.
fixes.replace: and the curtains there are flowered.
fixes.why: "Have flowers on them" is clunky for "в цветочек."

fixes.find: "Who are you looking for, Grandpa?"
fixes.replace: "Who are you looking for, sir?"
fixes.why: A stranger calling him "Grandpa" sounds wrong in English; Russian дедушка is a polite address.

fixes.find: The last thing I see is the light going out in my window.
fixes.replace: In my window, the light goes out.
fixes.why: Avoids the stock death-frame "the last thing I see" while keeping the final detail.

fixes.find: We never had curtains with flowers.
fixes.replace: We never had flowered curtains.
fixes.why: Matches the corrected idiom and reads naturally.

verdict: Партия в целом сильная: финальная сцена держит холод и ясную геометрию шва, голос старика в основном выдержан. Чаще всего мешают русские синтаксические кальки, неточные бытовые реалии по глоссарию и отдельные неанглийские словосочетания. Самые важные фактические вещи — часы, 04:12, 252, шрам — сохранены.
